intent: Compare the shares of U.S. adults reporting that economic conditions were hurting versus not hurting them and their families.

basis.entity: Economic conditions hurting them and their families
Economic conditions not hurting them and their families (implied complement)

units.claim: Among U.S. adults, a smaller share reported that economic conditions were hurting them and their families (46%) than reported that conditions were not hurting them (54%).

basis.entity: Economic conditions hurting them and their families
Economic conditions not hurting them and their families (implied complement)

accept: not hurting share exceeds hurting share by 8 percentage points
hurting share is lower than not hurting share
reject: hurting share exceeds not hurting share
the comparison uses a different population or unit

optional_valid: The two shares sum to 100% because the not-hurting category is the implied complement.
The chart is a snapshot with no time trend.
unsupported_to_avoid: Claiming a temporal change or trend in the shares.
Claiming geographic variation across states from the tile map.
Claiming a causal relationship between economic conditions and survey responses.
Treating the implied complement as an independently surveyed category rather than a derived complement.
review_notes: Only one analytical slot is required: the hurting-versus-not-hurting share comparison.
The not-hurting value is an implied complement (100 - 46 = 54), so the comparison is supported by both listed rows.
approval_basis: Human sampling review completed; remaining items approved as a batch.
